item.caption:
From Washington City to Logan, Utahns showed up Saturday for the fourth nationwide “No Kings” day of protests — but this time, participants voted, too.

The demonstrations were meant to mobilize people to cast their midterm ballots early ahead of Election Day on Nov. 3, organizers said.

In Salt Lake City, protesters marched from the Capitol to a ballot drop box by Salt Lake City’s Main Library.

Around two thousand people gathered at the Capitol ahead of the march, filling the steps with American flags, protest signs, music and costumes — and a recurring message that change starts at the ballot box. Many in the crowd had already voted, but some who brought their ballots proudly waved them in the air.

🔗: Read more at the link in our bio.

(✍️: Samantha Moilanen | 📹: @LandwehrPhotography)

item.caption: 🚨 BALLOT INTEGRITY: California Outlaws Arrests Within 200 Feet of Polling Locations on Election Day 🚨  Governor Gavin Newsom enacts a dedicated buffer zone designed to insulate voters from intimidation at the ballot box.  Key takeaways from the signed measure:The Legislative Buffer: California Governor Gavin Newsom formally signed a statute that criminalizes or bars law enforcement arrests within 200 feet of any voting site on Election Day.  Addressing Voter Intimidation: The law aims to prevent operations by law enforcement or immigration agencies (such as ICE) near voting precincts that could deter eligible citizens from turning out.  Visual Flashpoint: Viral posts juxtaposed Newsom against tactical agents wearing "POLICE ICE" gear, framing the legislation as a shield for vulnerable and immigrant communities against aggressive enforcement.  The National Debate: Voting rights advocates celebrate the rule as a vital safeguard ensuring unimpeded civic participation, whereas conservative critics argue that restricting law enforcement jurisdiction near public buildings could hinder response efforts during genuine criminal activity. 💬 Do you view this 200-foot buffer as a necessary protection against voter intimidation, or does it limit law enforcement too broadly? We need more accessible arts opportunities to bring people together, encourage civic participation, and help communities feel heard and represented. 🎭💙

By investing in the arts, we can create more spaces for people to share their stories, connect with others, and engage with the issues that shape their lives.

New Hampshire's Secretary of State asked the Supreme Court to bar poll workers from even considering a college student's ID on Nov. 3. Two federal courts have already said no to pausing the order against that directive.

item.caption:
Per un italiano abituato a raggiungere il seggio nei giorni stabiliti per una consultazione, il sistema americano può apparire insolito. Infatti, quando arriva l’Election Day, una gran parte degli elettori ha già votato, perchè negli Stati Uniti, la partecipazione al voto può distribuirsi su diverse settimane, attraverso modalità disciplinate dai singoli Stati.

In Florida le possibilità sono tre: votare personalmente in anticipo, richiedere una scheda da compilare a casa e restituire il plico in persona presso uno dei seggi allestiti o per posta, oppure presentarsi al seggio nel giorno delle elezioni. Anche il voto anticipato, dunque si svolge in presenza.

Questa flessibilità consente di organizzarsi intorno agli impegni quotidiani. Chi lavora su turni, assiste un familiare o prevede di essere fuori città il 3 novembre può scegliere un’altra giornata, senza dover concentrare tutto nell’appuntamento conclusivo.

L'articolo completo su italiareportusa.com.

#florida #miami #usa #electionday #politics

Gen Z for @sherrod 🤝 Millennial for @sherrod

KNOW BEFORE YOU GO: Voting Checklist

If you’re heading to the polls, take a moment to prepare before you go!

A few reminders to help make your voting experience as smooth as possible:

✅ Bring your photo ID. Make sure you have an acceptable form of identification with you.

✅ Know your ballot. Take a few minutes to review your sample ballot before arriving so you know what to expect.

✅ Double-check your ballot. Before making your selections, take a moment to confirm that the ballot you receive matches your voting location and the election you’re there to vote in. If something doesn’t look right, ask an election official for assistance before proceeding.

✅ Take your time. Review your selections carefully before submitting your ballot.

Your voice matters, and every voter deserves the opportunity to cast their ballot accurately and confidently.

Thank you for being an engaged part of our community. 🇺🇸

#KnowBeforeYouGo #ColumbiaTN #MauryCounty #ElectionDay

San Mateo County has delivered vote-by-mail ballots, and today, Monday, October 19, is the deadline to register or update your voter information. Visit smccd.edu/registertovote to register, check your status and find other voting resources.

🗳️🇺🇸 I VOTED ON THE FIRST TODAY OF EARLY VOTING AND BILL VOTED TODAY! 🗳️🇺🇸

For me, voting is personal. It is part of my family legacy of civic engagement, courage, faith, and service.

My Sanders, Bell, and Penny families have a history of civil rights activism and standing up for our community.

My mother, Ida Smith Sanders, was a precinct chair, and my brother served on the Clayton Town Council.

item.caption:
I went out to vote on the very first day of early voting here in San Antonio, and what I thought would be a relatively quick trip turned into nearly FOUR HOURS of waiting in line near Northwest Vista College.

I’m glad I got to cast my ballot, but there’s no reason voting should take that long. We should be making it easier for Texans to vote, especially when so many people have jobs and other responsibilities that make waiting in line for hours difficult.

As I say every election year, I always encourage everyone to do their own research on the candidates and issues on the ballot. Take some time to look into who’s running, what they believe in, and what they’re actually proposing to do if elected.

Of course, as your CD 20 representative on the State Democratic Executive Committee, I’m proudly supporting Democrats up and down the ballot this November! I’m especially proud to have cast my vote for Clayton Tucker for Texas Agriculture Commissioner. As someone who currently works on his campaign’s communications, I’ve gotten to see firsthand how hard he works and how committed he is to fighting for everyday Texans. I’m proud to be part of his team and even prouder to have voted for him!

Early voting is underway, y’all! Make a plan to vote, check the wait times at your polling location if they’re available, and don’t forget to bring a little patience with you!

#IVoted #TexasVotes #EarlyVoting #TexasDemocrats #Election2026
